title: Shortest Path to Get All Keys

reported.text: Shortest Path to Get All Keys in a grid (BFS over position plus key bitmask), written on paper with a dry run.

sources.passage:
PhonePe OA + Interview Experience (2025 Campus Hiring)
I recently went through the PhonePe hiring process (OA + 3 rounds) and wanted to share my experience.

OA:
There were 4 questions, 2 from DP, 1 from Trees, and 1 was a bit different.
The last one was: given a number in the form of a string (length up to 47) and an integer B, we can pick digits from the string (in order) to form numbers. The task was to count how many numbers greater than B can be formed.
Out of the 4, I could fully solve 2 and partially solve the other 2. I still got shortlisted.

Round 1 (Technical):
Both questions were from LeetCode –

Burning Tree

Shortest Path to Get All Keys

I had to write the complete code on paper and also dry run it. The round lasted around 1 hour 10 minutes. I was able to answer both.

Round 2 (HM round):
This was more ad-hoc. I gave my best but the interviewer didn’t seem fully convinced. Luckily I still made it to the next round.

Round 3 (Technical):
Two problems again –

Codeforces 2028C

A custom problem: given a vector of pairs (a, b), you can pick any pair to start with. The next pair must satisfy a_next <= b_prev. The goal was to maximize the sum of all chosen b.

The constraints weren’t specified, so after discussing I suggested bitmask DP for small n (around 12–20). The interviewer asked me to proceed, and I wrote the solution on paper. Both problems were solved.

Feedback from both technical rounds was good, and by Shri Krishna’s grace I got shortlisted at the end.

title: Substrings With Equal Vowels and Consonants

reported.text: Count the substrings of a lowercase string that contain equal numbers of vowels and consonants.

sources.passage:
PhonePe | SDE Intern | Interview Experience
Recently I had the oppourtunity to go through the recruitment process of **PhonePe** for the **SDE Intern** position for the summer of 2027 (Location - Bangalore/Pune). I'm sharing the problems here for anyone who might find it helpful!

### Tehnical Round - 1
It was fully based on DSA (2 problems were asked). No other discussion whatsoever. We were supposed to write the code on paper. 

1. This exact problem: https://leetcode.com/problems/shortest-bridge/description/

2. You are given an array of length n, where each element represents the coverage range of that index. If you choose an index i with value > 0, it covers all positions from i - value to i + value (inclusive), with the coverage clipped to the array boundaries. The chosen element also covers itself as part of this range. And, if arr[i] = 0, choosing that index provides no coverage at all, including not covering itself. Your task is to select the minimum number of indices such that every position in the array is covered by at least one selected index. If it is impossible to cover the entire array regardless of which indices are chosen, return -1. 

    Here's the LC equivalent : https://leetcode.com/problems/minimum-number-of-taps-to-open-to-water-a-garden/description/

### Technical Round - 2
Again, fully based on DSA.

1. You are given a string consisting of lowercase English letters ('a'–'z'). A substring is said to be balanced if it contains an equal number of vowels and consonants. The vowels are {a, e, i, o, u}, and every other lowercase letter is considered a consonant. Your have to determine the total number of balanced substrings in the given string.

2. This exact problem: https://leetcode.com/problems/shortest-path-in-a-grid-with-obstacles-elimination/description/

PhonePe | Interview Experience | SDE (intern + full time)
Location : Banglore
Position : SDE intern + fulltime

**Round 1:**
1. You are given an array of strings arr. A string s is formed by the concatenation of a subsequence of arr that has unique characters.
Return the maximum possible length of s.

**Example:**
```
Input: arr = ["uniq", "characters", "only", "please"]
output: 4
```

2. Find all possible recipes from given supply.

**Example:**
```
Input: recipes = ["bread","sandwich"],
       ingredients = [["yeast","flour"],["bread","meat"]],
       supplies = ["yeast","flour","meat"]
Output: ["bread","sandwich"]
```

**Round 2:**

1. Given a string and an integer k, find the length of the longest substring that contains k or fewer characters that are the same.

**Example:**

```
Input: s = "aabccbb"
       k = 2
Output: 5
```
2. Given a list of employees and their email addresses, write a function to find the departments to which each employee belongs based on the domain of their email address. The department name is the part of the email address after the '@' symbol.

**Example:**
```
Input: employees = [Employee("John", "john@example.com", ""), 
                    Employee("Jane", "jane@example.com", ""), 
                    Employee("Jim", "jim@example2.com", ""), 
                    Employee("Jill", "jill@example.com", "")]
Output: 
Department: example.com
  Employee: John
  Employee: Jane
  Employee: Jill
Department: example2.com
  Employee: Jim		 
```

**Round 3: HR interview**

They asked about 
1. My project 
2. Previous internship 
3.  Why phonepe
4.  and someother few questions.

Result: Not Selected
